lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Fabiola, it's Marisol from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not great. My knees have been bothering me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's hard to think about goals when your body isn't cooperating.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to walk 20 minutes on 4 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It went really well, I actually did it 4 times.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar is lower in the morning when I walk after dinner.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After dinner I can walk the dog, she needs it anyway.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Fabiola, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Marisol. Bye!

tags.note: Knee pain mentioned; minor, not explored further
Commits to doing it this week
Repeats advice already given without permission
Plans phone alarm; husband makes it easier
Motivation to keep up with grandkids
Plans morning walk before other tasks

flags.reason: Repeats the same advice after participant gave lukewarm response, without asking permission; MI non-adherent.
Advice given immediately after offering to share an idea, pushing a specific suggestion before exploring the participant's own ideas.

score.summary: Marisol drew out real change talk, including a concrete goal of a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days, and offered autonomy at goal-setting. However, she repeated advice at line 22 after Fabiola showed reluctance, and never explored the knee pain or affirmed her four completed walks.
strengths: Line 10 and 12: accurate reflections that captured Fabiola's willingness and noticed benefit.
Line 14: asked permission before sharing an idea.
Line 39: 'It's completely your call' reinforced autonomy at goal-setting.
Line 31 and 40: open questions about what would make walking easier and what might get in the way.
coaching_tips: Line 22 repeated advice that Fabiola had already received at line 16; instead reflect her barrier ('Between appointments there was no time') and ask what might work.
Line 9: affirm the four completed walks directly ('You did it four times, that's real effort') before moving on.
Line 6: briefly ask about the knee pain and whether it affects the walking plan, rather than moving past it.
Line 30: respond to 'At least I'm trying' with an affirmation or reflection of her effort and motivation.
Line 42: summarize the agreed goal and barriers before closing, and confirm the new call time from her request for a later slot.
